points.description: Initialisation: arranges the weights/neurons in the required topology (lattice) and initialises the weights randomly (all different); then samples an input vector from the input space.
Similarity matching: finds the winning neuron in the lattice for the sampled input (best match, e.g. minimum distance).
Weight update: updates the weights of the winning neuron and its neighbours, as determined by the neighbourhood function.
Shrinks the neighbourhood and decays the learning rate; repeats sampling until ordering and convergence are complete, then stops.
